classification_signals: This is the first book to consider these new scientific and humanistic models in architectural terms. (page 2)

Constructed as a series of five essays around the themes of beauty, culture, emotion, the experience of architecture, and artistic play, this book draws upon a broad range of discussions taking place in philosophy, psychology, biology, neuroscience, and anthropology, and in doing so questions what implications these discussions hold for architectural design. (page 2)

The essays collected here compose a series of initial attempts to survey the new models currently being put forth in the sciences and humanities concerning our human natures, with particular relevance to architecture. (page 21)
Discussion of historical and contemporary theories (Dalcroze, Lipps, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Gibson, neuroaesthetics, mirror neurons) and their implications for design.
title: Architecture and Embodiment: The Implications of the New Sciences and Humanities for Design

minimum_safe_summary: This book, "Architecture and Embodiment," by Harry Francis Mallgrave, is a theoretical exploration of how recent discoveries in the biological sciences and humanities can inform architectural design. It argues that traditional dualistic views of mind and body are obsolete, proposing instead that humans are embodied beings whose minds, bodies, environment, and culture are deeply interconnected and continually shape our understanding of the world. Key findings include the idea that environments restructure cognitive abilities, emotions precognitively inform our responses, and mirror neurons enable embodied simulation of the physical environment. The book advocates for shifting architectural focus from objectification to the human experience, considering how design elements impact perception, emotion, and behavior. A stated limitation is that current neuroimaging technologies confine studies to motionless conditions, though this is expected to change.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Cognition is deeply dependent on features of the physical body and the environment, rather than being an abstract process.
Mirror neurons facilitate understanding of others' actions and intentions by simulating them, and this mechanism extends to how individuals perceive and interact with architectural spaces.
The mirror neuron system plays a crucial role in empathy, social cognition, and the perception of affordances in the environment.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper proposes that architectural environments, through their physical properties, engage the embodied cognitive system, including mirror neurons, leading to changes in cognitive abilities and outlooks.
